title: Support Engineer, U.S. Government Support
description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role
As a Support Engineer on our U.S. Government Support Engineering team, you operate at the critical intersection of Support and Engineering, enabling public sector organizations and United States government agencies to run GitLab in some of the most secure and constrained environments in the world. Your work directly supports national security missions, including customers operating within FedRAMP-authorized, air-gapped, and classified or semi-classified environments where traditional troubleshooting approaches are not always possible.

In this role, you will engage deeply with GitLab through the command line; analyzing logs, system behavior, and application performance with strong Linux fundamentals and an understanding of how GitLab’s components interact end-to-end. You may partner with Product and Engineering to reproduce and document edge-case defects using sanitized or redacted data, or contribute directly to the product by opening merge requests that resolve customer-impacting issues. Beyond resolving individual cases, you’ll help strengthen GitLab by improving documentation, support workflows, and institutional knowledge, ensuring that lessons learned in highly regulated environments benefit the broader platform; all while working in a fully remote, highly collaborative environment built on trust, autonomy, and shared ownership.

Some examples of our projects:

A tool to quickly analyze strace output
A solution to capture the state of a customer’s server for easier troubleshooting
A functionality to ChatOps to make it easier to identify user accounts on GitLab.com

What you’ll do

Collaborate closely with public sector customers, including U.S. government agencies, the Department of War, and Intelligence Community organizations, to diagnose, troubleshoot, and resolve complex issues in GitLab deployments operating under strict security, compliance, and operational constraints.
Perform deep, hands-on technical investigations using Linux command-line tooling and GitLab internals to analyze logs, system performance, and application behavior, often with limited telemetry or incomplete datasets. You will trace issues across infrastructure, application, and code paths to identify root causes, recommend mitigations, and drive durable fixes; frequently partnering with GitLab Product, Development, and Infrastructure teams to ensure outcomes that meet both mission and platform reliability requirements.
Create and update clear, reusable documentation and support content based on real customer interactions to improve self-service and reduce repeated issues.
Participate in regular pairing sessions with other Support Engineers and act as a stable counterpart to cross-functional teams to share knowledge and improve support processes.
Contribute to building and refining internal support tools and workflows, including automation and troubleshooting utilities, to make diagnosing and resolving issues more efficient.
Participate in weekday and weekend on-call rotations, providing timely emergency support for self-managed customers operating in restricted and compliance-focused environments.
Support the growth of the team by reviewing applications and assessments, and participating in interviews and hiring decision discussions.

What you’ll bring

Due to government security requirements, you must be a United States Citizen (defined as any individual who is a citizen of the United States by law, birth, or naturalization) to be eligible for this position
Experience managing customer-facing cases across the full support lifecycle, from initial inquiry and triage through reproduction, escalation, and resolution
Strong Linux systems administration knowledge, with the ability to troubleshoot performance and configuration issues in complex environments
Familiarity with AI/LLM-powered developer tooling and gateway architectures (for example GitLab Duo, AI gateway configurations, or similar model-serving/proxy layers), including how they're deployed and troubleshot in self-managed or air-gapped environments
Ability to use scripting languages (preferably Ruby or Bash) and work within model-view-controller frameworks (preferably Ruby on Rails) to investigate and resolve issues
Practical experience with Git and continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) workflows
Skill in creating and maintaining clear, accurate support content and technical documentation
Ability to explain complex technical topics in a clear, empathetic way to customers and coworkers with varying technical backgrounds
Familiarity with DevOps practices and container-orchestration technologies such as OpenShift and Kubernetes
Understanding of common information security and compliance concepts and controls (for example DISA STIG and SELinux), and eligibility to work on United States federal customer environments as required for this role

About the team

At GitLab Federal, LLC, the U.S. Government Support Engineering team partners with public sector organizations and United States government agencies to support GitLab in highly secure, mission-critical environments. Our work directly enables national security outcomes, supporting customers across the Intelligence Community, Department of War, and other federal, state, and local government entities operating within regulated and restricted boundaries.

We are embedded within Support Engineering and work closely with Product, Development, Infrastructure, Customer Success, and Sales to solve complex, high-impact technical challenges. Our team frequently dives into code, logs, and architectural behavior to understand not just what is failing, but why; especially in environments with sanitized data, limited visibility, and strict compliance controls such as FedRAMP. We collaborate asynchronously across time zones and through structured pairing and discussion to share knowledge, strengthen solutions, and continuously improve how GitLab supports secure, air-gapped, and regulated deployments, while upholding GitLab's standards for rigor, transparency, and technical excellence.

The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. See more information on our

title: Logistics, Administration, and Finance (LAF) Officer
description:
About Us

Help Generation (HG) is a women-led, non-profit local NGO registered with the Ministry of Justice of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia (Certificate No. 4459). HG maintains a strong regional presence across Tigray, Amhara, Oromia, Southern Ethiopia, Afar, and Addis Ababa. Our mission focuses on Protection, Education, Livelihood Development, and Humanitarian Emergency Response.

With UNICEF support, HG is implementing the GBV and Child Protection Preparedness and Response Plan in conflict- and drought-affected woredas. As part of scaling up operations in Afar, HG seeks a dedicated Program and Finance Officer to strengthen program delivery and financial accountability.

Position Summary & Job Purpose

The Logistics, Administration, and Finance (LAF) Officer will ensure effective coordination between program implementation and financial management. The role supports planning, budgeting, reporting, and compliance, enabling transparent and efficient delivery of project activities. Operating under the direct supervision of the Regional Project Manager, the officer will manage program budgets, oversee financial documentation, and provide technical support to field teams.

Key Responsibilities

Program Management

Support program teams in activity planning, indicator tracking, and reporting.
Monitor project implementation and ensure alignment with donor requirements.
Prepare narrative and quantitative progress reports for submission to the Regional Project Manager.
Facilitate coordination with woreda-level government offices and partner organizations.

Financial Management

Prepare, review, and reconcile monthly financial reports in compliance with HG and donor standards.
Ensure timely cash flow projections, payroll compliance, and budget monitoring.
Review and authorize financial transactions in line with organizational policies and donor codes.
Maintain accurate financial documentation and ensure audit readiness.

Administration & Compliance

Uphold HG’s Code of Conduct, PSEA Policy, and Child Safeguarding Policy.
Support procurement processes and ensure compliance with HG and donor guidelines.
Maintain strict confidentiality and data protection protocols for all financial and program records.

Organizational Safeguarding & Misconduct Statement

HG has zero tolerance for sexual exploitation, abuse, harassment, child abuse, and other forms of misconduct. All staff must comply with HG’s safeguarding policies and complete mandatory PSEA and child safeguarding training.

Diversity & Inclusion

HG is committed to diversity, inclusion, dignity, and equal opportunity. Women, persons with disabilities, and qualified candidates from local communities are strongly encouraged to apply.

title: EPIDEMIOLOGY ACTIVITY MANAGER- Addis Ababa
description:
Defining, designing, coordinating, supervising, analysing and communicating on the epidemiological activities ensuring the development of appropriate methodologies in line with MSF standard tools and protocols. He/she contributes to the mission/project strategy regarding epidemiological and medical activities.

Defining, scheduling and organizing, in close collaboration with other medical team members, the annual epidemiological activity plan as well as its associated budget, in order to improve early detection of risk factors to better define treatment approaches and preventive practices. Leading the implementation of the protocols and epidemiological methodology, ensuring all related staff follows them in order to improve the epidemiology activities efficiency.
Supervising, according to annual plan, the epidemiological activities ensuring that contacts with community groups and authorities are aligned with the objectives of the those activities . Reporting on the progress of data collection, on ongoing analysis or on any issue causing delay, in order to achieve epidemiological goals on time.
Defining in coordination with the MSF medical team on epidemiological activities that would contribute to the MSF social mission (eg. Surveillance, surveys, research, advocacy,).
Supervising the implementation of epidemiological activities (including for example data filing procedures), ensuring that all epidemiology software tools are properly used and are updated regularly, in order to ensure full data traceability and availability
Ensure that the outcomes/results of the epidemiological activities are analyzed, contextualized and used for the MSF social mission
Planning and supervising, in close coordination with the HR department and the MSF vision, policies and values, the associated processes (job description, recruitment, training, performance evaluation, development and internal/external communication) of the epidemiological staff in order to ensure both the sizing and the amount of knowledge required, to improve staff technical capabilities, contribution and commitment to MSF values.
Participating in operational reports and organizing and/or assisting medical staff in preparing epidemiological reports
The epidemiology activity manager should also assume the responsibilities of the Epidemiologist if required (view Epidemiologist job description).
Ensuring and maintaining technical collaboration with the Epidemiology Advisers in the Medical Department (HQ).
Participating in workshops organised by the Medical Department (HQ) on topics related to the Epidemiology domain.

While the final responsibility of the quality and analysis/interpretation of the routine data should remain on the PMR/MedCo, the Epidemiology Activity Manager could provide feedback and should work together with PMR/MedCo to improve the quality or the analysis/interpretation of the routine data.

Lead and strengthen integrated disease surveillance systems at project level (Begi Hospital, PHC sites, mobile clinics, and community level), ensuring early detection of epidemic-prone diseases such as malaria, cholera, measles, and malnutrition.
Develop and implement outbreak detection thresholds, alert mechanisms, and rapid response tools in line with the mission’s emergency preparedness strategy and recurrent outbreak context.
Ensure real-time data collection, analysis, and interpretation to inform medical decision-making, particularly in high-burden areas with malaria outbreaks, GAM rates, and communicable diseases.
Support the integration of surveillance into PHC, ICCM, and community-based activities, including population mapping, MUAC screening, and malaria test-and-treat strategies.
Coordinate and strengthen community-based surveillance systems, working closely with health promotion, community health workers, and MoH structures to improve early warning capacity.
Ensure data quality assurance systems (collection tools, databases, validation processes) are in place and regularly monitored to improve reliability and usability of epidemiological data.
Provide regular epidemiological analysis and reporting (weekly/monthly) to inform operational priorities, including outbreak response, mobile clinic deployment, and resource allocation.
Contribute to emergency preparedness planning (E-prep) by developing epidemiological scenarios, projections, and indicators to guide contingency planning and response strategies.
Collaborate with medical teams to monitor key indicators across services (OPD, IPD, nutrition, SRH, vaccination), ensuring alignment with project objectives on reducing morbidity and mortality.
Support operational research and innovation opportunities within the mission, including studies on disease burden, access to care, and effectiveness of interventions.
Work closely with MoH and partners to align MSF surveillance systems with national systems, contributing to capacity building and sustainability.
Provide technical support and training to national staff on epidemiology, surveillance tools, outbreak investigation, and data use for decision-making.
Ensure epidemiological support to mobile and hard-to-reach areas, adapting tools and approaches to insecure and access-constrained environments.
Monitor and analyze population dynamics (IDPs, refugees, host communities, mining populations) and their impact on disease patterns and health service needs.
Contribute to advocacy efforts by providing evidence-based data on disease burden, access constraints, and protection of health facilities and populations.

Ensure close collaboration with logistics and supply teams to anticipate needs for outbreak response (RDTs, medications, sampling materials) based on epidemiological trends.

No. of positions: 01
Place of work: MSF- Switzerland-Coordination office, Addis Ababa
Position holder report to(direct supervisor): Medical Coordinator/ Medical Project Referent
Length of contract: till 30 June 2027
Remuneration and Benefits:
Starting Base salary (N+0) –USD 1806, payable in Ethiopian Birr (ETB).
Medical cover: as per the organization's policy

title: Regional Project Coordinator – Resilient Borderlands
description:
About HEKS/EPER

Swiss Church Aid (HEKS/EPER) is the aid organization of the Swiss Protestant Churches. It works toward a more humane and just world, supporting people and communities to overcome economic, social and humanitarian disparities and to live with dignity and greater self-determination. HEKS/EPER works in development cooperation, humanitarian aid and social inclusion and is a member of the ACT Alliance. HEKS/EPER’s work is guided by justice, self-determination, solidarity, responsibility, participation, proximity to people and effective action. Its international priorities include climate justice, the right to land and food, flight and migration, and inclusion.

About the project

Resilient Borderlands is a regional, multi-partner initiative across the Karamoja Cluster and adjacent cross-border areas of Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda and South Sudan. The project aims to improve the preventive and adaptive capacity of targeted communities to climate-induced conflict by strengthening existing local peace and climate actors, inclusive governance structures, cross-border cooperation and community-driven action. The project combines climate adaptation and peacebuilding through community-led, conflict-sensitive, human rights-based, gender-transformative and youth-responsive approaches. It will support locally led initiatives, strengthen the leadership of women, young people and marginalised groups, and generate evidence and knowledge for learning, advocacy and scale-up. Bread for the World is the project’s main financing partner.

Purpose of the position

The Regional Project Coordinator reports to the Programme Manager, and provides overall coordination and day-to-day leadership for the project across all four countries. The position is the central link between HEKS/EPER, implementing partners, Bread for the World, and key stakeholders, ensuring that the consortium works as one programme, delivers agreed results, complies with contractual requirements and continuously learns and adapts. The Coordinator will provide strategic direction, facilitate collective decision-making, track performance and risks, and promote accountability across the consortium. The role requires excellent management skills, capacity to influence, diplomacy and sound judgement: country teams and partners retain responsibility for implementation in their respective areas, while the Coordinator ensures coherence, quality and timely delivery at regional programme level.

Project countries

Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda, South Sudan

Duty station

Addis Ababa, frequent travel across the project countries

Reports to

Programme Manager

Contract period

One year with possibility of extension

Key relationships

Bread for the World, HEKS/EPER country and global teams; implementing partners; relevant authorities and regional stakeholders

Key responsibilities

Regional project leadership and coordination
Coordinate implementation across Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda and South Sudan, ensuring coherence with the proposal, results framework, budget, donor, and government agreements.
Lead joint planning, review and adaptive management processes with HEKS/EPER country teams and implementing partners.
Maintain an overview of progress, deliverables, risks and key decisions, addressing bottlenecks and escalating major concerns where required.
Ensure regional coherence while allowing implementation to respond to different country contexts and community priorities.
Monitor implementation against agreed workplans, targets, budgets and timelines, identify delays or underperformance, and coordinate corrective actions with country teams and implementing partners.
Ensure that changes in conflict, climate and security dynamics are reflected in project planning, risk management and adaptive management decisions across the four countries.
Provide line management, supervision and performance support to designated project staff, as required, ensuring clear responsibilities, effective teamwork and timely delivery of agreed priorities.
Consortium governance and partner coordination
Coordinate project governance bodies, meetings, decisions and follow-up actions.
Maintain effective communication, information sharing and working arrangements among HEKS/EPER offices implementing partners, and key stakeholders.
Promote collaboration, mutual accountability, local ownership and timely problem-solving across the consortium with deliberate efforts in coordinating with and engaging local administrations .
Support partners in meeting their programmatic, financial, safeguarding, visibility and reporting obligations.
Relationship with Bread for the World and donor compliance
Serve as the principal operational contact between HEKS/EPER and Bread for the World, in coordination with relevant HEKS/EPER management.
Coordinate donor communication, meetings, reporting and follow-up actions.
Lead the consolidation and quality assurance of narrative , financial and government reports and other contractual deliverables.
Ensure that donor requirements and relevant HEKS/EPER policies are understood and applied across the project.
Coordinate requests for approval of significant changes through the appropriate HEKS/EPER channels.
Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning (MEAL)
Ensure that the project maintains an integrated, community-led and conflict-sensitive approach to climate adaptation and peacebuilding.
Promote the consistent integration of gender equality, youth leadership, disability inclusion, safeguarding and accountability.
Work with technical and MEAL colleagues to harmonise monitoring systems, review project performance and support evidence-based adaptation.
Coordinate learning processes, evaluations and the development of knowledge products, including case studies, policy briefs and learning papers.
Facilitate cross-country exchange, joint learning and consistent application of agreed approaches.

5. Financial oversight, grants and risk management

Maintain a programme-level overview of expenditure, forecasts and budget variances in collaboration with finance colleagues and budget holders.
Facilitate regular programme and financial reviews and follow up on significant variances or compliance concerns.
Oversee the consistent and transparent application of the community-managed microgrant mechanism.
Maintain the regional risk register and monitor agreed mitigation measures in close coordination with the finance manager(s) and other Key Members of the consortium.
Support audits, evaluations and compliance reviews by ensuring that required documentation is complete and accessible.

6. Safeguarding, security and representation

Promote compliance with safeguarding, prevention of sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment, anti-fraud, complaints and whistleblowing requirements.
Refer safeguarding or integrity concerns immediately through the appropriate confidential channels.
Coordinate with country management and security focal points to ensure that travel and regional activities follow applicable security procedures.
Represent the project, when delegated, in relevant national, regional and cross-border forums.
Build constructive relationships with authorities, IGAD, civil society, donors and other relevant stakeholders.
Represent the project in policy and advocacy platforms and contribute to positioning project evidence and lessons within relevant national, regional and international discussions.

7. Fundraising and other tasks

Occasionally support fundraising, proposal development and other organisational priorities, as requested by the Head of Programmes, relevant Country Directors, GAP Advisor, or the line manager.
Lead project exit and closure in accordance with HEKS/EPER and donor requirements.
Undertake other duties consistent with the purpose and seniority of the position.

title: EUDR Compliance & Traceability, Coffee Certification Officer  (or Agricultural GIS and Certification Officer)
description:
About Us

Fahem General Trading PLC is a premier dual-sector supplier specializing in critical agricultural and veterinary inputs, including Coffee Processing Mesh. In response to global market demands and international trade regulations, we are seeking a highly technical, data-driven, and detail-oriented EUDR Compliance & Traceability Officer to lead our coffee sustainability, geolocation mapping, and European Union Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) compliance strategies.

Key Responsibilities

Geolocation & GPS Mapping: Collect, organize, and manage precise GPS coordinates for all coffee-producing farm plots. Ensure smallholder farms (<4 hectares) are mapped with single points and larger estates (>4 hectares) are accurately mapped using polygon boundaries.
Satellite Deforestation Screening: Utilize GIS tools and satellite imagery to verify and audit that sourcing farm lands have not undergone deforestation or forest degradation after the December 31, 2020 cut-off date.
Coffee Crop Growth Monitoring: Utilize satellite data and field audits to monitor coffee crop development, vegetation health, and seasonal growth stages.
Digital Traceability Management: Implement and oversee a robust digital supply chain tracking system from the farm level, through coffee washing stations, up to final export shipping. Enforce strict segregation protocols to prevent compliant coffee from mixing with unverified sources.
Local Legal Compliance Verification: Audit and document that all coffee sourcing lands possess legal tenure, adhere to local environmental protection laws, and respect labor and farmers' rights according to Ethiopian legislation.
EU Due Diligence Execution: Prepare and submit comprehensive Due Diligence Statements into the European Union's designated IT system prior to export, and manage the tracking of official EUDR Reference Numbers.

Fahem General Trading PLC

Position

EUDR Compliance & Traceability, Coffee Certification Officer
(or Agricultural GIS and Certification Officer)

Employment Type

Full-Time

Location

Addis Ababa (with field travel to coffee sourcing areas)

6 working days from the date of this announcement

title: STOREMAN (ENGINEERING DPT)
description:
Location/Duty Station: Benishangul Gumuz, Asosa Zone, Kurmuk Woreda Project Site
Roster: Fly-In/Fly-Out (6 Weeks On / 2 Weeks Off)
Company: Kurmuk Gold Mine PLC (KGM), a subsidiary of Allied Gold Corp
Employment Type: Full-Time | Site-Based

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Storeman (Engineering DPT) is responsible for the safe, accurate, and efficient receipt, storage, control, and issue of engineering materials, spare parts, tools, consumables, and maintenance-related equipment required for mining and processing operations. The role ensures that engineering inventory is properly identified, stored, preserved, recorded, and readily available to support planned and breakdown maintenance while maintaining accurate stock levels, warehouse housekeeping, and compliance with KGM Health, Safety and Environmental standards and inventory procedures.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

A. Engineering Stores Operations

Receive, inspect, identify, and verify engineering materials, spare parts, tools, equipment, and consumables against approved purchase orders, delivery notes, and specifications.
Ensure received materials are correctly counted, labelled, coded, and recorded before being placed into storage.
Store engineering items in designated locations according to their type, size, value, condition, and storage requirements.
Issue spare parts, tools, lubricants, consumables, and other engineering materials against authorized requisitions or work orders.
Ensure materials issued to maintenance teams are correctly recorded and traceable.
Maintain orderly and efficient storage of mechanical, electrical, instrumentation, welding, hydraulic, pneumatic, and other engineering materials.
Ensure critical and high-value spare parts are properly secured and controlled.
Maintain appropriate storage conditions for items requiring special protection, including bearings, electrical components, seals, chemicals, lubricants, and other sensitive materials.

B. Inventory Control and Stock Management

Maintain accurate inventory records for all engineering stock and ensure physical stock agrees with system records.
Monitor minimum, maximum, and reorder levels and communicate potential shortages of critical engineering spares.
Conduct regular stock counts, cycle counts, and physical inventory checks as required.
Investigate and report stock discrepancies, damaged materials, obsolete items, and unidentified stock.
Apply appropriate stock rotation principles, including FIFO/FEFO, where applicable.
Monitor slow-moving, obsolete, surplus, and non-moving engineering materials and provide information for management review.
Maintain accurate records of stock movements, transfers, issues, returns, and adjustments.
Support the identification and control of critical spare parts required to maintain plant availability and operational continuity.

Maintenance and Engineering Support

Provide timely support to Engineering and Maintenance teams by ensuring required spare parts, tools, and consumables are available when needed.
Prepare and issue materials for planned preventive maintenance, shutdowns, major maintenance activities, and breakdown repairs.
Coordinate with Maintenance Planners, Supervisors, Engineers, and Procurement teams regarding material requirements and availability.
Support the identification of alternative or equivalent spare parts where approved and within established procedures.
Receive and process returned or unused materials from maintenance activities and ensure they are inspected, identified, and returned to the correct storage location.
Maintain appropriate stock levels of frequently used maintenance items to minimize operational delays.
Assist with preparation of material kits for planned maintenance and shutdown activities.

D. Materials Identification and Preservation

Verify part numbers, descriptions, specifications, quantities, and condition of engineering materials before storage or issue.
Maintain proper identification and labelling of spare parts and materials to prevent incorrect issue or installation.
Ensure engineering materials are protected against corrosion, contamination, moisture, dust, deterioration, and other forms of damage.
Monitor shelf life and condition of materials where applicable and report items requiring preservation, replacement, or disposal.
Maintain manufacturer documentation, certificates, technical specifications, manuals, and other relevant material records where required.
Ensure materials are stored according to manufacturer recommendations and site procedures.

Warehouse Safety and Compliance

Follow all KGM warehouse, engineering, HSE, security, and inventory control procedures.
Conduct required inspections of storage areas, racks, lifting equipment, tools, and material-handling equipment.
Maintain safe access, appropriate stacking, clear walkways, and proper segregation of materials.
Use appropriate PPE and safe material-handling techniques when receiving, moving, storing, and issuing materials.
Operate forklifts, pallet jacks, lifting equipment, or other material-handling equipment only when trained and authorized.
Properly segregate and control hazardous, flammable, chemical, and environmentally sensitive materials in accordance with site requirements.
Report hazards, incidents, damaged materials, unsafe storage conditions, and near misses promptly.
Maintain high standards of housekeeping within engineering stores, laydown areas, and associated storage facilities.

ERP, Documentation and Reporting

Enter and maintain accurate material receipts, issues, transfers, returns, and stock adjustments in the approved ERP/inventory management system.
Maintain accurate bin locations, stock codes, descriptions, quantities, and material status.
Process authorized material requests, reservations, issues, and returns in accordance with established procedures.
Maintain documentation including purchase orders, goods received notes, material requisitions, issue vouchers, transfer documents, and other inventory records.
Prepare routine stock and inventory reports as required by the Stores or Supply Chain Supervisor.
Provide accurate information on stock availability, shortages, critical spares, and outstanding material requirements.
Maintain complete and traceable records to support internal controls and audits.

Coordination and Communication

Coordinate closely with Engineering, Maintenance, Procurement, Supply Chain, Finance, and other relevant departments.
Communicate material shortages, delivery delays, discrepancies, damaged goods, and urgent requirements promptly.
Support Procurement and Supply Chain teams with accurate information on stock availability and historical consumption.
Participate in regular meetings, inventory reviews, stock counts, and maintenance planning activities as required.
Maintain effective communication during shift handovers to ensure continuity of stores operations.
Perform other duties related to engineering stores and materials management as assigned by the Supervisor.

title: Terms of Reference (ToR)   Event Organizer for Annual Energy Event
description:
Terms of Reference (ToR)

Event Organiser for Annual Energy Event

Position Title: Event Organiser (Firm)

Location: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

Duration: September – November 2026 (tasks delivered on a rolling basis)

Reporting to: Communications Officer & Finance and Admin Manager, EWiEn

1. Background

The Ethiopian Women in Energy (EWiEn) is hosting its Annual Energy Event, a flagship gathering that brings together government representatives, private sector actors, exhibitors, development partners, media outlets, and other stakeholders. The event is a dynamic platform that promotes inclusive energy development, facilitates knowledge sharing, showcases innovations, and recognises outstanding contributions to the sector.

To ensure the successful delivery of this high-profile event, EWiEn seeks to engage a professional Event Organiser. The selected firm will be responsible for managing the full scope of event logistics, from planning, print vendor procurement, exhibitor coordination, media management, and videographer facilitation to on-site execution, AV/screen management, real-time event documentation, and post-event reporting. The Event Organiser will operate independently with minimal supervision from EWiEn, ensuring a seamless experience for all participants, sponsors, exhibitors, and media partners.

2. Objective of the Assignment

The Event Organiser will oversee the overall coordination, logistical arrangements, print procurement and material handling, exhibitor setup, media management, videography support, screen and AV monitoring, on-site management, real-time session note-taking, and post-event reporting for the Annual Energy Event. The firm will ensure timely preparation, effective stakeholder communication, flawless execution, and thorough post-event documentation.

3. Key Responsibilities

Planning, Coordination & Administrative Liaison

Lead overall implementation of the Annual Energy Event in close coordination with EWiEn.
Maintain regular alignment with EWiEn’s Admin and Finance team to ensure smooth execution of operational logistics, including catering arrangements (lunch/refreshments), venue seating layouts, and payment processing.

description:
Addis Eyita is a private company that provides business and investment consulting services, business training and intellectual advice in various fields of work, and import and export firms, and was established in January 2007 based on the Ethiopian Commercial Law. The company wishes to employ a qualified Import Export Accountant for its Power Import Export firm.

Job Summary

The Chemist will be responsible for the formulation, testing, and quality assurance of soap and detergent products. A key function of this role is to design and deliver hands-on training programs to production staff, technicians, and designated personnel on the safe and correct preparation of soap and detergent formulations. The ideal candidate will combine strong technical chemistry expertise with excellent instructional and communication skills.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

A. Training & Instruction (Primary Focus)

Develop comprehensive training curricula, manuals, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) for soap and detergent preparation.
Conduct practical, hands-on training sessions on the step-by-step manufacturing processes, including:
Soap preparation: saponification, cold/hot process methods, ingredient measurement, curing, and molding.
Detergent preparation: surfactant blending, builder incorporation, pH adjustment, viscosity control, and finishing.
Train staff on proper handling, measurement, and mixing of raw materials (e.g., oils, fats, alkalis, surfactants, fragrances, dyes, preservatives).
Instruct trainees on the correct use and maintenance of laboratory and production equipment.
Assess trainee competency through practical demonstrations, written tests, and on-the-job evaluations.
Provide refresher training and advanced workshops as needed.
Maintain accurate training records and issue certificates of completion.

B. Formulation & Product Development

Develop, optimize, and scale up soap and detergent formulations to meet product specifications and market requirements.
Source, evaluate, and approve raw materials and chemical ingredients.
Conduct compatibility and stability testing of formulations.
Research and introduce new formulations, eco-friendly alternatives, or cost-effective ingredient substitutions.

C. Quality Control & Assurance

Perform routine chemical analyses and physical testing on raw materials, in-process samples, and finished products (e.g., pH, viscosity, foaming capacity, total fatty matter, active matter content, microbiological testing).
Investigate and resolve product defects, inconsistencies, or deviations from specifications.
Ensure all products comply with relevant national and international standards (e.g., ISO, GMP, local regulatory requirements).

D. Health, Safety & Compliance

Train all personnel on chemical safety, hazard communication (SDS/MSDS), proper use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), and emergency procedures.
Ensure all preparation and production activities comply with occupational health, safety, and environmental regulations.
Manage proper storage, labeling, and disposal of chemicals and waste materials.

E. Documentation & Reporting

Prepare and maintain batch records, formulation sheets, training logs, test reports, and technical documentation.
Generate regular reports on training progress, quality metrics, and production issues for management review.

title: Android Software Engineer
description:
About ActAI

There are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks, calendar and they're not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal prompting.

Our product focuses on achieving high reliability for long-running workflows, persistent context, and real-world task completion. We believe products will greatly reduce hallucinations

Our objective is to organise anyone's life, allowing us all to spend time on valuable and meaningful things.

Role

As an Android Software Engineer, you own the Android client experience, how AI feels, behaves, and performs on mobile devices. This is not a thin client role. You will build a production Android application where AI interactions are core to the product, and performance, reliability, and clarity matter.

Focus

Build and maintain production Android apps using Kotlin.

Integrate AI-powered features (chat, vision, voice, recommendations) via backend APIs.

Design UX patterns for AI interactions, including streaming responses, retries, and partial results.

Optimize performance, memory usage, and responsiveness for AI-heavy flows.

Implement analytics, logging, and feedback capture to support AI evaluation and iteration.

Collaborate closely with backend and ML engineers on API contracts and system behavior.

Ensure app stability, security, and scalability in production environments.

Ideal Experiences

3+ years of Android development experience using Kotlin.

Hands-on experience integrating AI features (e.g. LLM, vision, speech APIs).

Strong understanding of asynchronous programming (Coroutines, Flow).

Familiarity with REST or gRPC APIs and structured data formats.

Strong debugging and performance profiling skills.

Comfort building in environments with latency, partial failure, and non-deterministic behavior.

Experience with MLKit or light on-device inference.

Published production apps on the Google Play Store.

Outcomes

Stable, smooth, and reliable real-world use android applications.

Performance is optimized: responsive, low-latency, and efficient on memory and CPU.

Production issues are detected early, monitored effectively, and resolved with clear root-cause analysis.

Tech Stack

Kotlin / Java

SQL / noSQL

TensorFlow Lite (on-device inference)

How We Work

The best products today in the world were built by small, world class teams. We are a high talent density and hands-on team. We make decisions collectively, move at rapid speed, striking a balance between shipping high quality work and learning. Joining our team requires the ability to bring structure, exercise judgment, and execute independently. Our goal is to put in hands of our users a truly magical product

Interview process

If there appears to be a fit, we'll reach to schedule 3, but no more than 4 interviews.

Applications are evaluated by our technical team members. Interviews will be conducted via virtual meetings and/or onsite.

We value transparency and efficiency, so expect a prompt decision. If you've demonstrated the exceptional skills and mindset we're looking for, we'll extend an offer to join us. This isn't just a job offer; it's an invitation to be part of a team that's bringing AI to have practical benefits to billions globally.

title: Consultant
description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

Location

This is a full-time position based in Munich or Cologne. Following a comprehensive onboarding period at our HQ in central Zurich (minimum one month), you will work from your home location, with occasional visits to customers across the DACH region.

As team collaboration is of great importance to us, we highly encourage team members to join us in Zurich at least once a month. These visits are financially supported by BLP.

About the role

For a process to run autonomously, four things have to line up: the technology, the process itself, the data behind it, and the people who work with it. That alignment does not happen at go-live. It happens in the months after, and that is where this role sits.

Our customers go live with a working solution. What they do not have on day one is an organisation that operates in an AI-native way. Processes were designed around people checking things. Data was maintained well enough for humans to interpret. Teams know the old workarounds better than the new system. Your job is to lead that transition, from a process that is automated in parts to a process that genuinely runs on its own.

That means working across every level of the customer's organisation. With operational teams you build understanding and find where automation is actually blocked. With department leads you challenge the process rules that make full automation impossible, and drive the decisions that change them. And you use the right lever for each blocker, because they are all different: some are a data clean-up you coordinate with the customer, some are a training and adoption gap, some need a custom agent, and some are structural and belong with our engineering teams.

You do not do this alone. You enable the customer's core team to solve their own issues, you work with our Customer Success Engineers on the technical side, and you use the Customer Success Manager to get decisions made where you need commercial weight. For our smaller customers, where there is no Customer Success Manager, you are the escalation point yourself.

You own customer health. Your sharpest measure of it is the automation rate.

What you'll do

Own customer health across your portfolio, measured first and foremost by automation rates.

Lead the transition to AI-native ways of working: identify what blocks automation, and pick the right way to solve each blocker.

Work with operational teams on enablement and adoption, so people work efficiently with blp rather than around it.

Challenge process rules that prevent automation, and drive improvements with the department leads who can decide.

Coordinate data clean-up with the customer where master data quality is capping what automation can reach.

Enable the customer's core team to resolve issues themselves, and reduce what has to come to us at all.

Identify where a custom agent solves the problem, and where the issue is structural and belongs with our engineering teams.

Collaborate with Customer Success Engineers on technical topics, and with the Customer Success Manager to get decisions made.

For customers without a Customer Success Manager, act as the escalation point for SLA breaches and own continuity of operations.

Direct the AI Automation Specialists working on your accounts.

What we're really looking for

The following key attributes ensure success in this role:

Process Excellence – You understand core business processes deeply, P2P and O2C, and you can see why a process is shaped the way it is and what it could look like instead.

Client Hands – You bring customers with you. You are strict on the things that matter and flexible on the things that do not, you understand the context people are working in, and you have more than one way of convincing them.

Ownership & Autonomy – You take a customer from live to high automation without being told the steps.

Comfort in the Data – You go into the numbers yourself to find where automation is leaking.

Problem Solving & Critical Thinking – You separate a configuration symptom from a process cause, and pick the right lever for each.

What you'll bring

Master's degree in Business, Finance, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.

3+ years of experience in consulting, process improvement, shared services, or ERP process ownership.

Deep working knowledge of at least one core business process end to end, purchase-to-pay or order-to-cash. This is a prerequisite, not a nice to have.

Demonstrable experience changing how a finance, procurement or supply chain team actually works, not only advising on it.

Strong analytical skills. You are comfortable working with process and transaction data directly.

Confident facilitating workshops with operational teams and presenting to their leadership.

Fluent in German and English, spoken and written.

Bonus points for experience with ERP systems, accounts payable or order management processes, or AI-driven SaaS.

What you'll get

High ownership environment – you shape your projects, outcomes, and career path.

Impact at scale – your work powers automation across global enterprises.

Cross-functional exposure – work with engineers, data scientists, and business leaders daily.

Real growth – fast-paced environment, steep learning curve, and structured career progression.

Employee ownership – be part of a majority employee-owned company with a best-in-class stock option programme.

Amazing team – become part of a driven and collaborative group of innovators.

Technology exposure – be at the forefront of emerging technologies and enjoy continuous learning opportunities.

Visits & offsites – paid visits and stays at our HQ in Zurich, including collaborative team offsites.

Ready to build the future of ERP automation? Join us and own your impact.

Learn more about blp and our values at .

title: Senior Creative Strategist
description:
About Sidekick

At Sidekick, we help people recover faster from injuries. Trusted by Olympic champions and everyday athletes, our products have been featured in Men's Health and Running Magazine. With 94% of users finding relief, we aim to be the go-to injury relief brand.

The role

A lot of performance creative work goes into creating demand that wasn't there. That's not the problem here. Our customer already wants what we sell. Their heel hurts every morning when they get out of bed, or their ankle rolls on uneven ground and they've stopped trusting it.

What they don't believe is that this is the thing that finally works. They've already bought the insoles, done the stretches, and gone to physio twice. So you have to teach before you can sell, and you have to earn trust from someone who has been let down already. It's a harder brief than most, and a more interesting one.

You'll write our paid social advertising and own angle development and testing, reporting to our Creative Director. Expect to ship around 15 briefs a week, a mix of net-new concepts and iterations on ads that are already working. Your week is writing, research, and feedback to editors.

You don't need a physiotherapy background, but you do need to pick up a clinical concept quickly enough to explain it clearly and honestly in fifteen seconds of camera time.

What you'll do

Find new winning angles. Better creative is what lets us spend more, so we need a steady supply of ads that keep working as budgets grow.
Open new audiences. Runners, older adults worried about falling, people on their feet all day. Each group buys for a different reason, and every one we crack opens up new demand.
Get more life out of winners. Read the data weekly, iterate what's working, retire what's finished.
Write the scripts. Short and long-form video, hooks that stop the scroll, dialogue that sounds like a real person. This is most of your week.
Direct the edit. Brief and manage editors and creators so the idea survives production.
Extend what wins. Take proven angles into landing pages and email.

Requirements

What we're looking for

4+ years writing paid social ads that were judged on sales (not brand awareness, engagement etc.)
Your ads have been responsible for over $100K+/month in ad spend (across all your ads, for a single brand). We'll ask you to walk us through it.
Proof you can iterate on a winner. Plenty of people can write one good ad; we want someone who gets eight more out of it.
You've opened a new audience before, and you can name the angle that got you in
Excellent writing for spoken word, which is a different skill from writing for the page
Strong direct response fundamentals: offer, mechanism, objection handling, proof
Experience briefing editors or creators
Health, fitness or medical device categories are a plus

What we care about

We want people who are ambitious and hold themselves to a high standard. They don't need to be managed closely, and want to be the best at their craft. The volume is real and the feedback is direct. In exchange you'll see more results in a year than most people see in three. If you're looking for something comfortable, this won't be the right fit for you.

Benefits

Compensation: Top of the market for this role. We’ll share compensation details on the first call.
Fast-growing company whose mission is to solve chronic pain and injuries
You’ll see the direct impact of your work on business results
You’ll be held to a high bar, which means you’ll get better fast
Fun, approachable yet ambitious colleagues
Comprehensive health benefits
Work from home

Excellent communication and negotiation skills in English (fluent) and Spanish , with a knack for navigating difficult conversations and maintaining long-term rapport.

Global client interaction in a dynamic company serving the market for 15+ years with offices in Antwerp, Lisbon, Viseu, Kyiv, Krakow, and New York.

title: Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP-BC) - Milford, MA
description:
Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP-BC) $135k - $160k/year

Position Requirement: Full-Time

FLSA Status: Exempt

Location: Milford, Massachusetts

Salary:

135K - 160K+

Work from Home! Competitive, negotiable salary! Work/life balance! Leadership and advancement opportunities!

Join a leading clinician-led behavioral health company today! OptiMindHealth (OMH) is expanding and seeking compassionate psychotherapists to join our team. Today, OMH provides superior behavioral health services patients in Massachusetts and Colorado. Since 2016, we’ve specialized in serving both adult and adolescent patients in a supportive outpatient environment. Our practice strives to improve access to holistic and cost-effective mental health care while supporting our clinical staff in all aspects of their work. Our clinicians define this work as the perfect balance between flexibility and efficiency.

OMH offers a variety of part-time and/or full-time options to our clinicians. Packages can be customized towards every clinician’s needs. Packages can include some combination of:

· Competitive Salary

· Medical benefits

· Paid malpractice policy

· CEU reimbursement

· Paid time off (PTO) and paid holidays

· Productivity Bonuses in select areas

· Work-Life Balance

· Flexible Work Schedule

No extra on call work, simply cover the care for your own patients!

It is common for clinicians to diversify their work today. Therefore, OMH’s flexibility and part-time options are the perfect complement to your professional and/or personal commitments. You can feel secure that OMH will offer steady, consistent income throughout your tenure.

Work from or close to home:

With locations in Colorado and Massachusetts, OMH is continuing to expand into states around the country. OMH will work with you to identify the best “fit” and will provide everything you need to treat OMH patients remotely from the comfort of your home. Our interview process focuses on your skill sets, interest as well as geographic location to match you to the best available option to begin working with OMH. Ask to speak with our recruitment team today to identify the local office(s) in your area, as well as those offices that are being planned for launch. Of course, if you prefer to work from home, we also have fully remote positions available.

Responsibilities:

The Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP-BC) will participate in the integrated care team model at OMH. Outpatient behavioral health practices like OMH are getting more attention than ever before due to the emphasis on team approaches. Join OMH to perfect your skills in the emerging field of integrated behavioral health care. The interdisciplinary health care team includes physicians, psychiatric nurse practitioners, licensed clinical psychologists, and licensed mental health professionals (LICSW/LPC/LMFT/LMHP). OMH values clinical relationships between all provider levels and believes this coordinated, collaborative approach provides the highest level of care to the patients we are privileged to serve.

Customize the care for each patient:

Our clinicians have the unique ability to customize the care for each and every individual patient. You will have the autonomy to determine how often you see a patient as well as the appropriate length of time spent with each patient. Medication management and individual psychotherapy are the most common forms of clinical work performed at OMH, but our clinicians also perform family therapy, group therapy, and psychological testing as needed and/or appropriate to a wide range of presenting problems of our patients.

Pick your own schedule!

Enjoy the freedom to create your own custom schedules with the perfect work/life balance.
Typically, clinicians work between Mondays – Fridays somewhere between the hours of 7:00 AM – 7:00 PM.

Focus on the patient’s care without the hassle or any additional on-call responsibilities. Simply cover the care for you own patients! Our medical staff and clinical psychotherapists focus on the patient’s care and our back-office support team handles the rest. This allows our clinicians time to be spent where it should be; with the patients they serve. Each clinician is responsible for clinical care and documentation following treatment sessions. Once that’s complete, our support team will handle all billing, collections, credentialing, etc. Once you leave the office for the day, your time is yours. No additional on-call responsibilities and no time spent wasted dealing with insurance companies.

Interested in benefits?

Full-time clinicians are eligible for medical health benefits. Please speak with the recruitment team to obtain additional specifics on benefits.

Leadership & Advancement:

OMH is a growing, clinician-led company. Our Site Supervisors are geographically dispersed throughout the areas we work in order to have staff leaders available to every clinician. Talk with our recruitment team today about the advancement opportunities to become senior psychotherapists and/or site supervisors.

Licensure, Education & Experience:

Licensure in Massachusetts as a Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner with experience working with persons who have various behavioral health issues such as, mood disorders, anxiety disorders, personality disorders, substance misuse, and other psychiatric impairments under the supervision of a consulting psychiatrist(s). We welcome new graduates!

Preferred: Successful completion of PMHNP-BC exam(s).

This document represents the major duties, responsibilities, and authorities of this job, and is not intended to be a complete list of all tasks and functions. Other duties may be assigned as well.

Salary: $135,000 – $160,000 / year

title: Missionary Team Leader
description:
Communitas is a church planting organization with 50 years experience working in Western Europe, Central and Eastern Europe, Latin America and North America. Our leading edge ministry is looking for the right person to help lead us into greater Kingdom ministry. Our current mission family of over 200 includes full-time, bi-vocational employees, as well as affiliates, with many of that number being non-Americans. Communitas operates in over 20 different countries as we start new initiatives and nurture churches and church-planting projects toward reproducible maturity.

Communitas is rooted in missional theology. Our three core values center on being Kingdom seeking, Grace oriented and People focused. Our church planting methodology is not tied to a specific formula, but rather the spirit of serving others and the embracing of a progression of actions that lead to a healthy, maturing church, making our approach very adaptable to unique contexts (see for details). We are pioneers and risk takers. We value honesty and encouragement. We collaborate well, within our global regions, as well as with partner organizations.

The Need and Opportunity

Across post-Christian secular culture people have largely given up on church, but spirituality remains important to them. Communitas International is at the forefront of sparking that spirituality with mission and helping people ‘taste and see that the Lord is good’. Our church planting organization offers the following:

A firm commitment to expressing the passionate love of God for the world in word and deed.
Substantial experience in reaching people in post-Christian culture.
Strategic coaching for planters and churches by experienced cross-cultural practitioners.
Robust training for team leaders and members via online cohorts, on-site events and regional/global seminars and conferences.
Rigorous assessment experiences and tools that can form the basis for strategic coaching and healthy team building.
Partnership in innovation with those looking for new ways to declare the timeless message of the Gospel.

Reports to:

Works closely with:

Local and/or cross-cultural clergy and lay ministry leaders

Location:

Typically outside USA

Classification:

Exempt

Clergy Status:

Yes, upon commissioning or ordination

Position Scope:

This pastoral role provides leadership, coaching, and mentorship to a team of missionaries while also serving as a lead church planter/missionary. The role is responsible for establishing and cultivating a missionally focused community of faith, guiding its growth from initial launch through long-term sustainability.

The planting pastor will utilize the proven methodology of the Communitas network of churches—embedding, initiating, practicing, maturing, hubbing, and extending—to shape the church’s formation, rhythms, and community life. This framework provides a foundation for healthy church development while allowing flexibility to adapt to the unique cultural context, needs, and opportunities of the local community.

The specific scope of responsibilities will vary according to the location, stage of church development, and ministry needs of the area served. The role requires both strategic leadership and contextual adaptability to foster a thriving, multiplying community of faith.

Principal Duties & Responsibilities:

Provide spiritual leadership, mentorship, and encouragement to team members while cultivating a culture rooted in faith and purpose.
Model a life of service, demonstrating a commitment to following Christ and embodying biblical principles in personal, relational, and ministry contexts.
Lead and support ministry decisions through prayerful discernment and alignment with biblical teachings, values, and the mission of the church.
Identify, recruit, develop, train, equip, and empower emerging leaders for effective ministry engagement and future church leadership.
Create and implement intentional evangelism strategies and outreach initiatives designed to engage the target community, build relationships, and support the launch and growth of a new church plant.
Perform additional responsibilities and ministry assignments as directed by the supervisor.

General Responsibilities:

Demonstrates spiritual maturity and a growing relationship with Jesus Christ.
Aligns fully with the mission, vision, values, and Statement of Faith of Communitas.
Demonstrates professionalism, discretion, and integrity in all matters.
Maintains a collaborative, learning-oriented, and positive leadership posture.
Commits to excellence in communication, stewardship, and organizational representation.

Qualifications:

A committed follower of Jesus Christ with a demonstrated personal faith, spiritual maturity, and a passion for advancing God’s mission.
Theologically grounded and in full alignment with Communitas’ Statement of Faith and positional papers.
A deep passion for sharing life with others through an incarnational, missional approach to ministry, with an understanding of group-based ecclesiology and emerging models of church.
An ability to understand, engage, and connect with the next generation of church communities while adapting ministry practices to diverse cultural contexts.
A strong awareness of the issues, needs, and worldview of contemporary postmodern culture, with the ability to communicate effectively and build meaningful relationships within that context.
Flexible, adaptable, and resilient, with the ability to navigate changing environments, evolving ministry needs, and new challenges.
A self-directed leader who demonstrates initiative, accountability, and the ability to work effectively both independently and collaboratively.
Proficiency with technology and digital tools, including Microsoft Office applications (Word and Excel), Zoom, Google Workspace, and other ministry-related platforms.
Prior church planting experience preferred, or significant training and experience in missional theology, church multiplication, and ministry practice.
Bachelor’s degree preferred.
Advanced theological education, seminary training, or equivalent ministry development experience is a plus.
Demonstrated success serving as a collaborative member of a high-functioning team, with the ability to build trust, contribute strategically, and support shared mission outcomes.

Funding:

This position is funded through personal ministry partnership development (support raising), which covers both salary and ministry-related expenses. Communitas provides onboarding, training, coaching, and ongoing support to help team members build and sustain a healthy ministry partnership team.

title: Senior Shopify Developer
description:
We are hiring a contract-based Senior Shopify Developer to contribute to our Design and Development Team.

Original Job posting link here

🌎About garden3d

We are worker owned creative collective, innovating on everything from brands and IRL communities to IoT devices and cross platform apps. We share profit, open source everything, spin out new businesses, and invest in exciting ideas through financial and/or in-kind contributions.

Our client roster includes Google, Stripe, Figma, Hinge, Black Socialists in America, ACLU, Pratt, Parsons, Mozilla, The Nobel Prize, MIT, Gnosis, Etsy & Gagosian.

We’re the software team behind innovative products like The Light Phone & Mill, and we operate a global, decentralized community space collective called Index Space.

We think of our garden3d as collective for creative people, prioritizing a happy, talented, and diverse studio culture. We work on projects that bring value to our world, and we balance deep care for the work we do with a genuine curiosity about life outside of our jobs.

Sanctuary Computer — Development At Sanctuary Computer we’re building a different type of technology shop – one that prioritizes close collaboration between the client and the craftsperson.

Our projects range from design-forward websites, to robust web apps, to native mobile development.

XXIX — Design When we started XXIX in 2013, we set out to create a different kind of design studio and we’ve thrived because we continually ask what a creative practice can be.

We’re building a radically different kind of organization that values autonomy, growth, transparency, and shared responsibility.

Lightphone

We're looking for a Senior Shopify Developer who balances deep e-commerce expertise with modern frontend engineering. You'll build pixel-perfect, hyper-performant storefronts ranging from custom Liquid themes to headless Hydrogen/Next.js implementations working alongside our design team to create world-class shopping experiences.

In this role, you’ll work across a variety of client projects to find cost-effective, high-quality, and pragmatic solutions to complex e-commerce challenges. Responsibilities will include:

Collaborating closely with Technical Leads and Designers to meet clients' custom e-commerce and technical needs.
Building and maintaining high-performance storefronts using both custom Liquid (Online Store 2.0) and modern headless architectures (Shopify Storefront API, GraphQL, Hydrogen/Remix, Next.js).
Implementing responsive, accessible, and pixel-perfect interfaces based on design specifications, with meticulous attention to product interaction details and motion design.
Integrating custom storefronts with headless CMS platforms (Sanity, Contentful), payment gateways, subscriptions, search, and third-party e-commerce APIs.
Optimizing e-commerce performance, focusing heavily on Core Web Vitals, image/video asset delivery, bundle size, and runtime efficiency across high-traffic collection and product pages.
Architecting scalable, reusable component libraries and design systems tailored for commercial platforms.
Writing clear documentation for store management, custom app integrations, and codebase maintenance.
Participating in project team rituals, including Sprint Planning, daily standups, code reviews, and retrospectives.

The person we’re looking for is happy, relaxed and easy to get along with. They’re flexible on anything except conceits that will lower their usually outstanding work quality. They work “smart”, by carefully managing their workflow and staggering features that have dependencies intelligently. They prefer deep work but are OK coming up to the surface now and then for top level / strategic conversations.

We believe people with backgrounds or interests in design, art, music, food or fashion tend to have a well rounded sense of design & quality, so a variety of hobbies or side projects is a big nice to have!

8+ years writing highly performant frontend code with an obsession for 95+ Lighthouse scores and optimal Core Web Vitals.
Deep Shopify Ecosystem Mastery: Proven experience building custom Shopify themes (Liquid, JSON templates, Online Store 2.0) as well as headless storefronts using the Shopify Storefront API (GraphQL) and frameworks like Hydrogen/Remix or Next.js.
Modern Frontend Tech: Expert-level experience with TypeScript and modern CSS methodologies (Tailwind CSS, CSS Modules) alongside robust animation libraries (GSAP, Framer Motion).
Headless CMS & Integrations: Extensive experience merging Shopify with headless CMS platforms like Sanity, Contentful, or Prismic, as well as third-party services (Klaviyo, Recharge, Algolia/Searchspring, Stripe).
Platform & Hosting: Fluency in industry-standard PaaS platforms including Vercel, Netlify, and Shopify Oxygen.
Architecture & State Management: Experience with state management solutions (Zustand, Redux, Pinia) and API integration patterns for cart state, multi-currency, and checkout flows.
Quality & Accessibility: Experience building accessible (WCAG compliant), responsive interfaces with a strong commitment to SEO best practices, testing frameworks (Jest, Playwright, Cypress), and maintainable code.
Performance Optimization: Practical knowledge of WebSockets, caching strategies (Redis, CDN-level/Cloudflare), and advanced image delivery networks.

💪 Nice-to-Have Competencies:

Custom App Development: Building bespoke Shopify Apps using Node.js, Remix, GraphQL Admin API, and Shopify CLI.
Shopify Plus & Enterprise Features: Hands-on experience with Shopify Functions, Checkout Branding API, Shopify Scripts, and B2B configurations.
Tracking & Analytics: Setting up server-side tracking, GTM, Meta Pixel, and Customer Privacy APIs without hurting site load times.
WebGL, Canvas & 3D: Experience building interactive graphics, 3D product visualizers, or canvas animations using Three.js or ``.
Full-Stack & API Design: Experience across backend/database layers (PostgreSQL), REST/GraphQL API design, and authentication flows (OAuth, JWT).
Client-Facing & Management: Direct experience working with clients to clarify requirements, defining product roadmaps, or leading engineering teams.

💸 Compensation

Our pay scale ranges from $40/hr to $120/hr pending seniority (& team leadership experience), and our projects are rarely less than 8 full time weeks at 40 hours per week.

We prefer long standing relationships with highly accountable and communicative team members, so we encourage candidates to expect longer term engagements.

🎤 How we interview

After you submit your application, a member of our team will reach out. Our interview process starts with an intro call to answer any questions you have about the role and to learn a bit more about your experience and interests.

From there, we’ll follow up with a panel interview call where you get to meet a few members of our team, to openly discuss some of our challenges and ensure your skills and interests align with where we’re going as a business.

For qualified candidates, the process wraps with a reference call, and an offer to follow.

title: Senior Independent Software Developer
description:
You must be located in the Americas, Europe, or Israel to apply.
A·Team is a VC-backed, stealth, application-only home on the internet for senior independent software builders to team up with hand-picked, high-growth companies on their next big thing.

After talking with hundreds of independent engineers, designers, and product folks, we heard over and over that finding vetted, high-quality, consistent clients is hard, and projects are often too small to be rewarding. A·Team matches small teams of the most talented builders in the world with companies backed by a16z, YC, Softbank, General Catalyst, etc. on a contract basis for many of their most important initiatives. We quietly launched in May 2020, and have helped A·Teamers earn $85+ million since.

As part of A·Team, you can expect:

High-paying, meaningful missions with the most audacious companies sent your way; generally $90-$150+/hr, with vetted, fascinating clients doing work that matters. We're picky about who we partner with; new clients only come in via trusted referral. We've worked with Lyft, McGraw Hill, ClearCo, Pepsi, Walmart, the former CEO of Waze, the leading vaccine production software, several new unicorns we can't say here, and dozens of startups backed by a16z/YC/Softbank/Insight/Tiger/etc.
Work alongside friends old & new: our niche is small/diverse product teams, since clients with larger budgets and higher-impact work tell us they want teams, not individuals. Of course, we keep friends together whenever we can.
Full autonomy: say "no" to things that don't excite you. The most talented builders often juggle a few things at once, so there's never pressure to join an A·Team mission if you don't have the bandwidth. If we're no longer a fit, it's easy to leave or pause too.
Small, curated, off-the-record gatherings: for conversations hard to have elsewhere. Long-term, we're creating micro-communities for the world's top builders to become friends around the things they care about.
Keep 100% of what you earn: if you charge $120/hr, you get $120/hr. A·Team makes money by charging a small, flat, transparent platform fee on top of your rate.

How to apply:

Go here: https://build.a.team/remotivereferral + mention Remotive. We respect your time so the application is short. We're also much more interested in seeing what you've made, and excited to chat more if there’s a fit.

What you’ll do:

Once part of A.Team, you’ll regularly be invited to impactful missions that match your interests. Find the right pick from early-stage incubations with world-class founders, to fast-growing super-funded companies, to old school non-tech incumbents looking to build as a tech giant would

Missions usually involve building an ambitious piece of software from 0 to 1 as part of a small 3-4 person team.

You’ll be paid to scope it out, give the client options, guide strategy, and execute on the selected solution. Sometimes the client has a clear vision, sometimes not; which is why A.Team builders tend to be senior folks who can work together to find the right direction.

Who A·Team is for:

Senior software developers who left large companies and high-growth startups to pursue their craft with autonomy.

Those who prefer consistent contract work over a full-time role, who want to create a variety of new products alongside other top-tier builders.

The majority of A.Teamers spend most of their time doing independent work, but a sizeable percentage are either employed full-time (but testing out client work), bootstrapping a side project, or looking for their next big thing

Who A·Team is not for:

People looking for small gigs

Folks looking to build simple wordpress/wix/squarespace-style websites

Those still early in their careers (<4 years) and recent university/bootcamp grads (at least not yet)

Our long-term vision:

A·Team is a new type of company for a new kind of independent software builder. We call them "unhirables": people who traditional companies couldn’t hire full-time even if they wanted to, but who want to do their most meaningful work with their favorite people in small, autonomous, distributed expert teams.

To help us secure amazing missions, we raised $60 million+ from Insight Partenrs, Tiger Global, NFX, RocNation, along with the former CEO of Upwork, the founders of Fiverr and Lemonade, Apple's Global Head of Recruiting, YC Partner Aaron Harris, Wharton's Adam Grant, and Duke's Dan Ariely.

Our Core Values

Dream Big, Then Make it Real
